summary: Vincenc Lesný was an Indologist who studied at the University of Prague and its Faculty of Arts (~1903–1909) under Moriz Winternitz and Josef Zubatý. He later held posts at both institutions from ~1924 to 1953.

Vincent Arthur Smith worked in Indology and history and archaeology, having studied at Trinity College Dublin (~1865–1871). He served in the Indian and Bengal Civil Services (1871–1900) and later held posts at the University of Oxford (~1910–1920).

Vincent Breugem specializes in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Lucia Dolce and at Hanazono, Taisho, Kyoto, and Leiden Universities, where he completed his MA and PhD and was attested as a research fellow in 2012.

Vincent Eltschinger specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Lausanne under Tom Tillemans, as well as Fribourg and Vienna. His posts include the Austrian Academy of Sciences, IKGA, and École Pratique des Hautes Études (~2015).

Vincent Goossaert works in Sinology and religious studies, having studied under Kristofer Schipper (~1993–1997). He held posts at CNRS (~1998–2012), The Chinese University of Hong Kong (2007), and École Pratique des Hautes Études (~2012).

Vincent Lefèvre specializes in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied under Bruno Dagens at the École Nationale des Chartes and Sorbonne Nouvelle University, and has served as a curator at the Musée Guimet.

Vincent Tournier is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Cristina Scherrer-Schaub, Seishi Karashima, and at EPHE and Leiden University, and was attested at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient in 2021.

Vincenzo Vergiani specializes in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Raffaele Torella (~1998–2004) and led a Sanskrit manuscript research project at the University of Cambridge from ~2014 to 2020.
Virendra Kumar Varma is an Indologist and linguist who studied under traditional teachers Ramnath Dixit and Gopal Chandra Mishra.
Virendra Kumar Verma is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ramanatha Dikshita and Gopal Chandra Mishra, and taught Kamala Prasad Mishra.

Virendra Nath Misra worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Lucknow (~1953–1957) and Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1958–1961), later serving as Director of Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1990–2000).

Vishva Bandhu worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as Founder-Principal of Dayanand Brahma Mahavidyalaya (1921), Director of Dayanand Anglo-Vedic College, Lahore (1934), and Director of the Vishveshvaranand Vedic Research Institute (~1935–1973).
Vishwa Nath Pathak was an Indologist and historian who studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He served as a professor at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University, attested in 1973–1978 and 1987.

Vishwanath Narayan Mandlik worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at Elphinstone College (~1847–1851), examined at the University of Mumbai, and was attested as Vice-President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai in 1878.

Vishwanath Prasad Varma is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He studied under Dhirendra Mohan Datta (~1942–1944), Ganga Nath Bhattacharya, doctoral supervisor Kali Kinkar Datta (~1947–1950), and Joachim Wach (1950).
Vitus Angermeier is an Indologist who studied under Karin Preisendanz, Chlodwig H. Werba, and Roque Mesquita.

Vladimir Minorsky worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and history and archaeology. He studied at Moscow Imperial University and Lazarev Institute, and held posts at INALCO (~1923–1932) and SOAS University of London (~1932–1944).

Vladimir Tikhonov specializes in history, archaeology, and religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at St. Petersburg, Korea, and Moscow State universities, and held posts at Kyung Hee University (1997–2000) and the University of Oslo (from 2000).

Vladimir Vyacheslavovich Balabushevich worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He was attested as Head of the Indian Department at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences in 1970 and 1990.
Volkbert Näther is an Indologist who completed his doctoral degree at the University of Marburg (attested 1975) under doctoral supervisor Claus Vogel.
